1. (Currently amended) An ultrasonic surgical instrument assembly comprising: a handpiece; a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece; a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator; and a light source removably attached to said handpiece so as to direct at least visible electromagnetic radiation along the probe towards a surgical site distal of the probe.

2. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1, further comprising a power supply mounted at least indirectly to said handpiece and operatively connected to said light source, wherein said power supply is electrically isolated from said transducer or generator.

3. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2 wherein said power supply includes a coil disposed about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator, and wherein said coil is operatively connected to said light source through a separate electrical circuit.

4. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 3 wherein said power supply further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil for providing energy or power to said light source for a predetermined period of time after termination of power conduction through said cable.

5. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2, further comprising a fastener for removably attaching said light source to said handpiece.

6. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 5, further comprising at least one additional fastener for removably attaching said power supply at least indirectly to said handpiece.

7. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 2, wherein said power supply is a battery operatively connected to said light source through a dedicated electrical connection independent of said transducer or generator.

8. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1 wherein said light source includes a light-emitting diode.

9. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1 wherein said light source is removably attached to a proximal or rear end of said handpiece, further comprising an optical fiber extending from said light source to a distal end portion of said handpiece.

10. (Currently amended) The surgical instrument assembly defined in claim 1 wherein said light source is removably attached to a distal end of said handpiece and is oriented to provide illumination along said probe to the surgical site.

11. (Currently amended) An accessory for a surgical instrument comprising a handpiece, a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece, and a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator, said accessory comprising: a light source; a fastener for removably attaching said light source to said handpiece; and at least one power supply component operatively connectable to said light source through a dedicated electrical circuit.

12. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said power supply component includes a coil disposable about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator, further comprising an additional fastener for removably attaching said coil about the power cable, and wherein said coil is operatively connected to said light source through a separate electrical circuit independent of said transducer or generator.

13. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 12 wherein said power supply component further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil and connectable to said light source for providing illumination energy to said light source for a predetermined period of time after a termination of power conduction through said cable.

14. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said power supply component includes a battery operatively connectable to said light source through a dedicated electrical connection.

15. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said light source includes a light-emitting diode.

16. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said fastener is configured for removably attaching said light source to a proximal or rear end of said handpiece, further comprising an optical fiber and at least one additional fastener for removably attaching said optical fiber to said handpiece so that said optical fiber extends from said light source to a distal end portion of said handpiece.

17. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said fastener is configured for removably attaching said light source to a distal end of said handpiece and for orienting said light source to provide illumination along said probe to a surgical site.

18. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 11 wherein said fastener is taken from the group consisting of a clip, a clamp, and a band.

19. (Currently amended) A surgical method comprising: providing a surgical instrument having a handpiece, a transducer or generator of ultrasonic mechanical vibrations disposed in said handpiece and a probe attached to a distal end of said handpiece and operatively connected to said transducer or generator; providing a light source; removably applying a fastener to said handpiece to attach said light source thereto so that light from said light source is directable along said probe; operating said surgical instrument to apply ultrasonic vibratory energy to a surgical site; during the operating of said surgical instrument, conducting electrical energy from a dedicated power supply to said light source through a circuit separate from said transducer or generator; and during the operating of said surgical instrument and the conducting of said electrical energy, illuminating said surgical site with light from said source.

20. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 19 further comprising removably mounting said power supply at least indirectly to said handpiece.

21. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 20 wherein said power supply includes a coil, the removable mounting of said power supply at least indirectly to said handpiece including disposing said coil about a power cable feeding said transducer or generator, and wherein said coil is operatively connected to said light source through a separate electrical circuit.

22. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 21 wherein said power supply further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil, further comprising operating said capacitor to provide illumination energy to said light source for a predetermined period of time after a termination of power conduction through said cable.

23. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 19, further comprising removably removing said fastener and said light source from said handpiece after completion of an operation on said surgical site.

24. (Currently amended) The surgical method defined in claim 19 wherein the removably applying of said fastener includes positioning said light source at a proximal or rear end of said handpiece, further comprising removably attaching an optical fiber to said handpiece so that said fiber extends from said light source at said proximal end of said handpiece to a distal end of said handpiece.

25. (Currently amended) An accessory for a medical instrument comprising a handpiece and a probe or tool extension on a distal end of said handpiece, said accessory comprising: a light source; a fastener for removably attaching said light source to said instrument; and at least one power supply component operatively connectable to said light source through a dedicated electrical circuit, said power supply component including a coil disposable about a power cable extending to said handpiece, further comprising an additional fastener for removably attaching said coil about the power cable, wherein said coil is operatively connected to said light source through a separate electrical circuit.

26. (Currently amended) The accessory defined in claim 25 wherein said power supply component further includes a slow-drain capacitor operatively connected to said coil and connectable to said light source for providing illumination energy to said light source for a predetermined period of time after a termination of power conduction through said cable.
